title: Local filesystem block store backend
description:
Implement FilesystemBlockStore storing one file per block in a configured directory, named by CID string. No network dependency. Intended for single-node deployments, development, and offline testing.

Depends on: pluggable backend epic (stoa-5c9f1a38).

## What needs doing

- Implement `FsStore: IpfsStore` (transit) and `FsBlockStore: IpfsBlockStore` (reader) using `tokio::fs`
  - `put`: compute CID locally, write `<path>/<CID>` atomically (write to `<CID>.tmp` then rename); skip if file already exists
  - `get`: read `<path>/<CID>`; map ENOENT → `None` / `NotFound`
- Add `[backend.filesystem]` config section: `path` (required), `max_bytes` (optional soft cap)
- IPNS: disable (log a one-time info message at startup that IPNS is not available with filesystem backend)
- Soft cap enforcement: if `max_bytes` is set, refuse `put` when the directory total exceeds the limit; return `WriteFailed` so the pipeline can shed load rather than silently filling disk
- Verify `path` exists and is writable at startup; fail fast if not
- Runbook section: recommended directory layout, disk sizing guidance, GC (manual or cron `find ... -mtime +N -delete`)

## GC / delete semantics

delete(cid) unlinks the file at <path>/<CID>. DeletionOutcome::Immediate — the file is gone as soon as unlink() returns. get() returns NotFound immediately after.

There is no grace period. The GC policy (max_age_days) is the operator's mechanism for ensuring articles are old enough before deletion. Operators who need a grace period should use the S3 lifecycle mode instead.

## Acceptance criteria
- Round-trip test: put a block, get it back, assert bytes match (no network required, uses tempdir)
- Atomic write test: simulate a crash mid-write (truncated .tmp file) and verify the block is absent (not partially present) after recovery
- Works on a fresh empty directory with no prior state
- delete() removes the file; get() returns NotFound immediately after
- delete() on a CID that does not exist returns Ok(DeletionOutcome::Immediate) without error (idempotent)
